Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment uses a substrate-trapping strategy to identify prolyl hydroxylation substrates. While PRIDE metadata lists 'Top-down proteomics', the methods describe trypsin digestion and LC-MS/MS on a Q-Exactive, which is characteristic of bottom-up proteomics. The primary goal is PTM (hydroxylation) site identification on ADSL Proline 24.

scope: Our screening combines the optimized substrate-trapping strategy with a TAP-TAG purification followed by mass spectrometry.
In parallel, we develop an orthogonal approach by combining this enzyme-substrate-trapping strategy to GST-EglN2 pull-down followed by mass spectrometry.

The EglN2 immunoprecipitates from MDA231 cells were eluted in 8 M Urea, reduced with 5 mM DTT and akylated with 15 mM IAA... followed by digestion by trypsin. The digests were desalted on homemade C18 tips and dried in speed-Vac. The clean peptides were dissolved in 0.1% Formic acid and ready for MS analysis.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics analysis was performed on material isolated via TAP-TAG purification and GST pull-down to identify EglN2 substrates, fitting the 'affinity-purified complex scope'.
